question: Should `operator.read` health recompute runtime-config drift from disk on every cache hit so restart-required auth/model/provider drift is immediately visible?
rationale: The code path is narrow and tested, but it deliberately trades cached health latency for fresher operator diagnostics and changes what read-scoped health reports about auth/provider config drift.

options.title: Accept immediate drift diagnostics
options.body: Land this diagnostic with exact-head CI refreshed, accepting the bounded disk read because stale auth/model drift is more harmful than the added health cost.

options.title: Narrow the recompute scope
options.body: Ask the PR to recompute drift only for admin/probe calls or add a small rate limit if cached health latency is more important than immediate read-scoped visibility.

options.title: Pause for restart-policy decision
options.body: Hold this diagnostic until the companion hot-mode restart-policy PR is decided if maintainers want diagnostics and behavior to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept immediate drift diagnostics
recommendation.body: Land this diagnostic with exact-head CI refreshed, accepting the bounded disk read because stale auth/model drift is more harmful than the added health cost.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the listed project maintainer and has recent history on gateway health and config runtime surfaces, making him the best owner for the health-latency tradeoff.
